newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields falls to 20.99 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields falls to 20.99 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs fell 101 basis points to 20.99 in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 20 billion bolivars of 180- day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with a 21.99 percent coupon for a price of 100.45 pct. At last week's auction the six month notes yielded 22.00 percent.

The bank also sold five billion bolivars of 269-day notes with a 22.58 percent coupon at a price of 99.10 percent, and five billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 23.19 percent coupon at an average price of 98.76 percent.
Yields for these notes fell 108 basis points to 24.00 percent for the 269-day bills, and 50 basis points to 24.75 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
